newsitem.title: TAIWAN: President abandons US$100m China project.
newsitem.headline: President abandons US$100m China project.

text.p: Taiwan's food giant President Enterprises said on Thursday it has abandoned its US$100 million power plant plan in China, and instead will invest more than T$30 billion in local projects in the next two years.
"President Enterprises cannot reach agreement with mainland China's counterparts, so we decided to abandon the planned US$100 million power project," company spokesman Yang Yu-pao told Reuters.

"Instead, we plan to expand our local investment," Yang said. "We plan to invest more than T$30 billion in the next two years to build two shopping malls and to enter medicine manufacturing as well," he added.

President Enterprise said last month it would delay its application for a power plant in the central Chinese city of Wuhan until the Taiwanese government set clearer guidelines for investments on the mainland.
The move followed an announcement by Formosa Plastics Group that it would call off a US$3.0 billion power plant project in China.
Taiwan President Lee Teng-hui said in August that the island needed to review its policy of targeting China as its main market and avoid over-dependence on the mainland for investment.
President is Taiwan's biggest investor in China, with investment totalling US$200 million in 15 companies there.
Yang said President planned to build two shopping malls in the southern Taiwanese cities of Kaohsiung and Tainan, and would invest T$900 million in pharmaceuticals.

Taiwan and China have been rivals since a civil war separated them in 1949. Although all investments in China must be government approved, Taiwan is still concerned that its economy may become too dependent on China.
Some 30,000 Taiwanese businesses have poured more than US$20 billion into China since the late 1980s.
